sanskrit: yadi brāhmaṇa dehas te nirātaṅko nirāmayaḥ aṅgāni ca samagrāṇi na ca lokeṣu dhikkṛtaḥ
english: If, O brāhmaṇa, your body is free of dread and free of disease, your limbs all whole, and you are nowhere scorned among the worlds,

sanskrit: na kena cit pravādena satyenaivāpahāriṇā dharmāyottiṣṭha viprarṣe nātmānaṃ tyaktum arhasi
english: and not by any rumor, however true and damaging — then rise up for the sake of dharma, O sage among the twice-born; you ought not to cast your self away.

sanskrit: yadi brahmañ śṛṇoṣy etac chraddadhāsi ca me vacaḥ vedoktasya ca dharmasya phalaṃ mukhyam avāpsyasi
english: If, O brāhmaṇa, you hear this and place your trust in my words, you will win the foremost fruit of the dharma declared in the Vedas.

sanskrit: svādhyāyam agnisaṃskāram apramatto 'nupālaya satyaṃ damaṃ ca dānaṃ ca spardhiṣṭhā mā ca kena cit
english: Vigilantly maintain your recitation of scripture and your tending of the sacred fire; uphold truth, self-restraint, and giving, and contend in rivalry with no one.

sanskrit: ye ke cana svadhyayanāḥ prāptā yajanayājanam kathaṃ te jātu śoceyur dhyāyeyur vāpy aśobhanam
english: Whoever are devoted to their own study and have attained to sacrificing and to officiating at sacrifice — how should they ever grieve, or brood upon anything unworthy?

sanskrit: icchantas te vihārāya sukhaṃ mahad avāpnuyuḥ uta jātāḥ sunakṣatre sutīrthāḥ sumuhūrtajāḥ
english: Seeking their delight, they would attain great happiness — born, moreover, under an auspicious constellation, at a holy ford, in a favorable hour.

sanskrit: nakṣatreṣv āsureṣv anye dustīrthā durmuhūrtajāḥ saṃpatanty āsurīṃ yoniṃ yajñaprasavavarjitām
english: Others, born under demonic constellations, at unholy fords, in an evil hour, fall into a demonic womb, bereft of the begetting of sacrifice.

sanskrit: aham āsaṃ paṇḍitako haituko vedanindakaḥ ānvīkṣikīṃ tarkavidyām anurakto nirarthikām
english: I myself was a petty pundit, a hairsplitting rationalist, a reviler of the Vedas, attached to the science of logic and the empty art of argument.

sanskrit: hetuvādān pravaditā vaktā saṃsatsu hetumat ākroṣṭā cābhivaktā ca brahmayajñeṣu vai dvijān
english: I was a proclaimer of disputatious doctrines, a speaker who argued with seeming reason in assemblies, a reviler and a contradicter of the twice-born at the offerings to Brahman.

sanskrit: nāstikaḥ sarvaśaṅkī ca mūrkhaḥ paṇḍitamānikaḥ tasyeyaṃ phalanirvṛttiḥ sṛgālatvaṃ mama dvija
english: A denier, doubting everything, a fool who fancied himself learned — and this, O twice-born one, is the ripening of that fruit for me: my jackal-state.

sanskrit: api jātu tathā tat syād ahorātraśatair api yad ahaṃ mānuṣīṃ yoniṃ sṛgālaḥ prāpnuyāṃ punaḥ
english: Might it ever come to pass, even after a hundred hundreds of days and nights, that I, a jackal, should attain the human womb again?

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭaś cāpramattaś ca yajñadānataporatiḥ jñeyajñātā bhaveyaṃ vai varjyavarjayitā tathā
english: Then, content and vigilant, delighting in sacrifice, giving, and austerity, I would become a knower of what should be known and one who shuns what should be shunned.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa munir utthāya kāśyapas tam uvāca ha aho batāsi kuśalo buddhimān iti vismitaḥ
english: Then the sage Kāśyapa rose up and said to him, marveling, "Ah, truly you are skilled and wise!"

sanskrit: samavaikṣata taṃ vipro jñānadīrgheṇa cakṣuṣā dadarśa cainaṃ devānām indraṃ devaṃ śacīpatim
english: The brāhmaṇa looked upon him with the far-reaching eye of knowledge, and beheld him to be Indra, lord of the gods, the consort of Śacī.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpūjayām āsa kāśyapo harivāhanam anujñātaś ca tenātha praviveśa svam āśramam
english: Then Kāśyapa did honor to the god borne by bay steeds, and, dismissed by him, he entered his own hermitage.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yady asti dattam iṣṭaṃ vā tapas taptaṃ tathaiva ca gurūṇāṃ cāpi śuśrūṣā tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: If there be giving, or sacrifice, or austerity practiced, and likewise the service of one's elders — tell me of this, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ātmanānarthayuktena pāpe niviśate manaḥ sa karma kaluṣaṃ kṛtvā kleśe mahati dhīyate
english: Bhīṣma said: Of itself, joined to ruin, the mind settles into evil; and that man, having wrought a defiled deed, is plunged into great affliction.

sanskrit: durbhikṣād eva durbhikṣaṃ kleśāt kleśaṃ bhayād bhayam mṛtebhyaḥ pramṛtaṃ yānti daridrāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ
english: From famine to famine, from affliction to affliction, from fear to fear, from the dead to deeper death — so the poor and the evildoers pass on.

sanskrit: utsavād utsavaṃ yānti svargāt svargaṃ sukhāt sukham śraddadhānāś ca dāntāś ca dhanāḍhyāḥ śubhakāriṇaḥ
english: From festival to festival, from heaven to heaven, from joy to joy they pass — the faithful, the self-restrained, the wealthy, the doers of good.

sanskrit: vyālakuñjaradurgeṣu sarpacorabhayeṣu ca hastāvāpena gacchanti nāstikāḥ kim ataḥ param
english: Through fastnesses of beasts of prey and rutting elephants, amid perils of serpents and thieves, the deniers go — bound at the wrists. What worse than this?

sanskrit: priyadevātitheyāś ca vadānyāḥ priyasādhavaḥ kṣemyam ātmavatāṃ mārgam āsthitā hastadakṣiṇam
english: But those dear to gods and guests, openhanded, friends of the good, have taken to the safe road of the self-possessed, where the right hand gives.

sanskrit: pulākā iva dhānyeṣu puttikā iva pakṣiṣu tadvidhās te manuṣyeṣu yeṣāṃ dharmo na kāraṇam
english: Like blighted grains among the wholesome, like winged ants among the birds, such are they among men for whom dharma is not the governing cause.

sanskrit: suśīghram api dhāvantaṃ vidhānam anudhāvati śete saha śayānena yena yena yathā kṛtam
english: Though a man run very swiftly, ordained destiny runs after him; it lies down beside him who lies down — in whatever manner each deed was wrought.

sanskrit: upatiṣṭhati tiṣṭhantaṃ gacchantam anugacchati karoti kurvataḥ karma chāyevānuvidhīyate
english: It stands beside him who stands, it follows him who goes, it acts upon him who acts — like a shadow it conforms to his deed.

sanskrit: yena yena yathā yad yat purā karma samācitam tat tad eva naro bhuṅkte nityaṃ vihitam ātmanā
english: By whatever means, in whatever manner, whatever deed a man has amassed before, just that he forever undergoes, ordained by his own self.

sanskrit: svakarmaphalavikṣiptaṃ vidhānaparirakṣitam bhūtagrāmam imaṃ kālaḥ samantāt parikarṣati
english: Scattered by the fruit of its own deeds, hedged about by ordinance, this host of beings Time drags onward from every side.

sanskrit: acodyamānāni yathā puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca svakālaṃ nātivartante tathā karma purākṛtam
english: As flowers and fruits, all unurged, do not overrun their proper season, so too the deed done long ago does not exceed its time.

sanskrit: saṃmānaś cāvamānaś ca lābhālābhau kṣayodayau pravṛttā vinivartante vidhānānte punaḥ punaḥ
english: Honor and dishonor, gain and loss, decline and rise — once set in motion, they turn back again and again as their ordinance runs out.

sanskrit: ātmanā vihitaṃ duḥkham ātmanā vihitaṃ sukham garbhaśayyām upādāya bhujyate paurvadehikam
english: Sorrow is appointed by oneself, joy is appointed by oneself; from the very bed of the womb onward, the deeds of a former body are undergone.

sanskrit: bālo yuvā ca vṛddhaś ca yat karoti śubhāśubham tasyāṃ tasyām avasthāyāṃ bhuṅkte janmani janmani
english: Whatever good or evil a man does as child, as youth, or as elder, that he undergoes in each such condition, birth after birth.

sanskrit: yathā dhenusahasreṣu vatso vindati mātaram tathā pūrvakṛtaṃ karma kartāram anugacchati
english: As among thousands of cows the calf finds out its mother, so the deed done before goes after the one who did it.

sanskrit: samunnam agrato vastraṃ paścāc chudhyati karmaṇā upavāsaiḥ prataptānāṃ dīrghaṃ sukham anantakam
english: A cloth, first soaked, is afterward made clean by labor; so for those purified by fasting there is happiness long and without end.

sanskrit: dīrghakālena tapasā sevitena tapovane dharmanirdhūtapāpānāṃ saṃsidhyante manorathāḥ
english: Through long-cultivated austerity in the penance-grove, for those whose evil has been shaken off by dharma, the heart's desires come to fulfillment.

sanskrit: śakunīnām ivākāśe matsyānām iva codake padaṃ yathā na dṛśyeta tathā jñānavidāṃ gatiḥ
english: As the track of birds in the sky cannot be seen, nor that of fishes in the water, so is the course of those who know the truth.

sanskrit: alam anyair upālambhaiḥ kīrtitaiś ca vyatikramaiḥ peśalaṃ cānurūpaṃ ca kartavyaṃ hitam ātmanaḥ
english: Enough of further reproaches and of transgressions recounted: what is fitting and seemly and good for the self — that is to be done.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kutaḥ sṛṣṭam idaṃ viśvaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam pralaye ca kam abhyeti tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Whence was this whole universe created, the world of things unmoving and moving, and into what does it pass at the dissolution? Tell me this, grandfather.

sanskrit: sasāgaraḥ sagaganaḥ saśailaḥ sabalāhakaḥ sabhūmiḥ sāgnipavano loko 'yaṃ kena nirmitaḥ
english: With its oceans, with its sky, with its mountains, with its clouds, with its earth, with its fire and wind — by whom was this world fashioned?

sanskrit: kathaṃ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni kathaṃ varṇavibhaktayaḥ śaucāśaucaṃ kathaṃ teṣāṃ dharmādharmāv atho katham
english: How were the beings created? How came the distinctions of the social orders? And how their purity and impurity, and how their right and wrong?

sanskrit: kīdṛśo jīvatāṃ jīvaḥ kva vā gacchanti ye mṛtāḥ asmāl lokād amuṃ lokaṃ sarvaṃ śaṃsatu no bhavān
english: Of what nature is the life-soul of the living, and whither go those who die? From this world to that world — let your honor declare it all to us.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam bhṛguṇābhihitaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bharadvājāya pṛcchate
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount an ancient tale — the excellent teaching spoken by Bhṛgu to Bharadvāja, who questioned him.

sanskrit: kailāsaśikhare dṛṣṭvā dīpyamānam ivaujasā bhṛguṃ maharṣim āsīnaṃ bharadvājo 'nvapṛcchata
english: On the peak of Kailāsa, seeing the great sage Bhṛgu seated and blazing, as it were, with splendor, Bharadvāja questioned him:

sanskrit: sasāgaraḥ sagaganaḥ saśailaḥ sabalāhakaḥ sabhūmiḥ sāgnipavano loko 'yaṃ kena nirmitaḥ
english: With its oceans, with its sky, with its mountains, with its clouds, with its earth, with its fire and wind — by whom was this world fashioned?

sanskrit: kathaṃ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni kathaṃ varṇavibhaktayaḥ śaucāśaucaṃ kathaṃ teṣāṃ dharmādharmāv atho katham
english: How were the beings created? How came the distinctions of the social orders? And how their purity and impurity, and how their right and wrong?

sanskrit: kīdṛśo jīvatāṃ jīvaḥ kva vā gacchanti ye mṛtāḥ paralokam imaṃ cāpi sarvaṃ śaṃsatu no bhavān
english: Of what nature is the life-soul of the living, and whither go those who die? Of this world and the next alike — let your honor declare it all to us.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa bhagavān pṛṣṭo bharadvājena saṃśayam maharṣir brahmasaṃkāśaḥ sarvaṃ tasmai tato 'bravīt
english: Thus questioned in his doubt by Bharadvāja, the blessed great sage, like Brahman in his radiance, then declared it all to him.

sanskrit: mānaso nāma vikhyātaḥ śrutapūrvo maharṣibhiḥ anādinidhano devas tathābhedyo 'jarāmaraḥ
english: There is a god renowned by the name of Mānasa (the Mind-born), of whom the great sages have heard of old — without beginning or end, indivisible, ageless and undying;

sanskrit: avyakta iti vikhyātaḥ śāśvato 'thākṣaro 'vyayaḥ yataḥ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni jāyante ca mriyanti ca
english: renowned as the Unmanifest, eternal, imperishable, undecaying — from whom the created beings are born and die.

sanskrit: so 'sṛjat prathamaṃ devo mahāntaṃ nāma nāmataḥ ākāśam iti vikhyātaṃ sarvabhūtadharaḥ prabhuḥ
english: That god first created what is called by name the Great One — renowned as Space (ākāśa) — the Lord who upholds all beings.

sanskrit: ākāśād abhavad vāri salilād agnimārutau agnimārutasaṃyogāt tataḥ samabhavan mahī
english: From space arose the waters; from the waters, fire and wind; and from the union of fire and wind there then came to be the earth.

sanskrit: tatas tejomayaṃ divyaṃ padmaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ svayaṃbhuvā tasmāt padmāt samabhavad brahmā vedamayo nidhiḥ
english: Then a divine lotus, made of splendor, was created by the Self-existent; and from that lotus arose Brahmā, the treasure-store made of the Vedas.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāra iti khyātaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtakṛt brahmā vai sumahātejā ya ete pañca dhātavaḥ
english: Brahmā, of exceeding splendor, is known as the I-principle (ahaṃkāra), maker of the inmost being of all creatures; and these are the five elements.

sanskrit: śailās tasyāsthisaṃjñās tu medo māṃsaṃ ca medinī samudrās tasya rudhiram ākāśam udaraṃ tathā
english: The mountains are called his bones, and the earth his marrow and his flesh; the oceans are his blood, and space, likewise, his belly.

sanskrit: pavanaś caiva niḥśvāsas tejo 'gnir nimnagāḥ sirāḥ agnīṣomau tu candrārkau nayane tasya viśrute
english: The wind is his breath, fire his bodily heat, the rivers his veins; the moon and the sun, Agni and Soma, are renowned as his two eyes.

sanskrit: nabhaś cordhvaṃ śiras tasya kṣitiḥ pādau diśo bhujau durvijñeyo hy anantatvāt siddhair api na saṃśayaḥ
english: The sky on high is his head, the earth his feet, the quarters his arms; hard to be known, because of his endlessness, even by the perfected ones — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: sa eva bhagavān viṣṇur ananta iti viśrutaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtastho durvijñeyo 'kṛtātmabhiḥ
english: That very one is the blessed Viṣṇu, renowned as the Endless (Ananta), dwelling as the inmost self of all beings, hard to be known by those of unperfected soul.

sanskrit: ahaṃkārasya yaḥ sraṣṭā sarvabhūtabhavāya vai yataḥ samabhavad viśvaṃ pṛṣṭo 'haṃ yad iha tvayā
english: He is the creator of the I-principle, for the coming-to-be of all beings; from him the universe arose — this is what you have asked of me here.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca gaganasya diśāṃ caiva bhūtalasyānilasya ca kāny atra parimāṇāni saṃśayaṃ chindhi me 'rthataḥ
english: Bharadvāja said: Of the sky and of the quarters, of the earth's surface and of the wind — what are their measures here? Cut away my doubt, truly and to the point.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca anantam etad ākāśaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam ramyaṃ nānāśrayākīrṇaṃ yasyānto nādhigamyate
english: Bhṛgu said: Endless is this space, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas, delightful, crowded with manifold abodes, whose end is not to be reached.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ gater adhastāt tu candrādityau na dṛśyataḥ tatra devāḥ svayaṃ dīptā bhāsvarāś cāgnivarcasaḥ
english: Above the range of their motion, beneath which the moon and the sun are not seen, there dwell gods self-luminous, shining, with the radiance of fire.

sanskrit: te cāpy antaṃ na paśyanti nabhasaḥ prathitaujasaḥ durgamatvād anantatvād iti me viddhi mānada
english: Yet even they, of famed splendor, do not behold the end of the heavens, by reason of its impassability and its endlessness — know this from me, O bestower of honor.

sanskrit: upariṣṭopariṣṭāt tu prajvaladbhiḥ svayaṃprabhaiḥ niruddham etad ākāśam aprameyaṃ surair api
english: Yet higher and higher still, by self-luminous blazing ones, this space is barred — immeasurable even by the gods.

sanskrit: pṛthivyante samudrās tu samudrānte tamaḥ smṛtam tamaso 'nte jalaṃ prāhur jalasyānte 'gnir eva ca
english: At the earth's end are the oceans; at the oceans' end darkness is held to be; at the end of darkness they declare there is water, and at the end of the water, fire.

sanskrit: rasātalānte salilaṃ jalānte pannagādhipaḥ tadante punar ākāśam ākāśānte punar jalam
english: At the end of the nether deep is water; at the water's end, the lord of serpents; beyond that again is space, and at space's end again water.

sanskrit: evam antaṃ bhagavataḥ pramāṇaṃ salilasya ca agnimārutatoyebhyo durjñeyaṃ daivatair api
english: Thus the end and the measure of the Blessed One, and of the waters too, drawn from fire, wind, and water, is hard to be known even by the gods.

sanskrit: agnimārutatoyānāṃ varṇāḥ kṣititalasya ca ākāśasadṛśā hy ete bhidyante tattvadarśanāt
english: The colors of fire, wind, and water, and of the earth's surface — these are like space itself, and are distinguished only by the seeing of truth.

sanskrit: paṭhanti caiva munayaḥ śāstreṣu vividheṣu ca trailokye sāgare caiva pramāṇaṃ vihitaṃ yathā adṛśyāya tv agamyāya kaḥ pramāṇam udāharet
english: And the sages recite in their various scriptures the measure ordained for the three worlds and for the ocean; but for that which is unseen and unattainable, who could set forth a measure?

sanskrit: siddhānāṃ devatānāṃ ca yadā parimitā gatiḥ tadā gauṇam anantasya nāmānanteti viśrutam nāmadheyānurūpasya mānasasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Since the course of the Siddhas and the gods is bounded, the name Ananta of the Endless One is renowned as figurative — fitting the title of the great-souled Mānasa whose appellation suits him.

sanskrit: yadā tu divyaṃ tadrūpaṃ hrasate vardhate punaḥ ko 'nyas tad vedituṃ śakto yo 'pi syāt tadvidho 'paraḥ
english: But when that divine form shrinks and again grows great, who else is able to know it, even were there another of like nature?

sanskrit: tataḥ puṣkarataḥ sṛṣṭaḥ sarvajño mūrtimān prabhuḥ brahmā dharmamayaḥ pūrvaḥ prajāpatir anuttamaḥ
english: Then from the lotus was created the all-knowing, embodied Lord, Brahmā — made of dharma, the first, the Lord of creatures, unsurpassed.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca puṣkarād yadi saṃbhūto jyeṣṭhaṃ bhavati puṣkaram brahmāṇaṃ pūrvajaṃ cāha bhavān saṃdeha eva me
english: Bharadvāja said: If he came to be from the lotus, then the lotus is the elder; yet your honor calls Brahmā the firstborn. Herein is my very doubt.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca mānasasyeha yā mūrtir brahmatvaṃ samupāgatā tasyāsanavidhānārthaṃ pṛthivī padmam ucyate
english: Bhṛgu said: That form of the Mind-born which here attained the state of Brahmā — for the purpose of providing it a seat, the earth is called the lotus.

sanskrit: karṇikā tasya padmasya merur gaganam ucchritaḥ tasya madhye sthito lokān sṛjate jagataḥ prabhuḥ
english: The pericarp of that lotus is Meru, towering into the sky; established in its midst, the Lord of the world brings forth the realms.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca prajāvisargaṃ vividhaṃ kathaṃ sa sṛjate prabhuḥ merumadhye sthito brahmā tad brūhi dvijasattama
english: Bharadvāja said: How does that Lord bring forth the manifold emanation of creatures — Brahmā, established in the midst of Meru? Tell me that, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca prajāvisargaṃ vividhaṃ mānaso manasāsṛjat saṃdhukṣaṇārthaṃ bhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ prathamato jalam
english: Bhṛgu said: The Mind-born brought forth the manifold emanation of creatures by his mind; and for the kindling-into-life of beings, water was created first of all.

sanskrit: yat prāṇāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vardhante yena ca prajāḥ parityaktāś ca naśyanti tenedaṃ sarvam āvṛtam
english: That by which the life-breaths of all beings thrive, and by which creatures, once forsaken of it, perish — by that is all this enveloped.

sanskrit: pṛthivī parvatā meghā mūrtimantaś ca ye pare sarvaṃ tad vāruṇaṃ jñeyam āpas tastambhire punaḥ
english: The earth, the mountains, the clouds, and whatever else has form — all that is to be known as born of the waters; for the waters then congealed.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca kathaṃ salilam utpannaṃ kathaṃ caivāgnimārutau kathaṃ ca medinī sṛṣṭety atra me saṃśayo mahān
english: Bharadvāja said: How was the water brought forth, and how the fire and the wind, and how was the earth created? Herein is my great doubt.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca brahmakalpe purā brahman brahmarṣīṇāṃ samāgame lokasaṃbhavasaṃdehaḥ samutpanno mahātmanām
english: Bhṛgu said: Of old, O brāhmaṇa, in the age of Brahmā, at an assembly of the great-souled brahmin-sages, there arose a doubt concerning the world's origin.

sanskrit: te 'tiṣṭhan dhyānam ālambya maunam āsthāya niścalāḥ tyaktāhārāḥ pavanapā divyaṃ varṣaśataṃ dvijāḥ
english: They remained, taking up meditation and holding to silence, unmoving — those twice-born ones, foregoing food and drinking only the wind, for a divine hundred years.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dharmamayī vāṇī sarveṣāṃ śrotram āgamat divyā sarasvatī tatra saṃbabhūva nabhastalāt
english: To the hearing of them all there came a voice made of dharma; there the divine Sarasvatī came into being out of the vault of heaven.
